stem: A 5-year-old boy presents with recurrent $Staphylococcus$ abscesses and $Aspergillus$ pneumonia. Which underlying immune defect is most likely?

options.text: Failure of neutrophils to undergo an oxidative burst.
Absence of the membrane attack complex ($MAC$).
Inability of leukocytes to adhere to vascular walls.

explanation: Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD) prevents neutrophils from killing catalase-positive organisms like $Staph$ and $Aspergillus$ due to a lack of reactive oxygen species.
rationale: The inability to kill 'catalase-positive' bugs is the hallmark of this condition.

optionExplanations.A: Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD) prevents neutrophils from killing catalase-positive organisms like $Staph$ and $Aspergillus$ due to a lack of reactive oxygen species.
optionExplanations.B: A $MAC$ deficiency (terminal complement) specifically predisposes individuals to $Neisseria$ infections, not typically $Staph$ abscesses.
optionExplanations.C: While antibody defects cause bacterial infections, the specific combination of deep-seated abscesses and fungal pneumonia ($Aspergillus$) strongly points toward a phagocytic defect.
optionExplanations.D: Leukocyte Adhesion Disorder (LAD) results in high blood counts and a lack of pus, whereas this patient has deep-seated abscesses and scarring.
